audits.title: EP-625 An audit looking at whether consent has been gathered to upload patient details to the National Vascular Registry in Countess of Chester Hospital
audits.standard: Consent for and upload of data to the National Vascular Registry
audits.setting: Vascular department, Countess of Chester Hospital

cycle1.result: Data uploaded to the NVR 42.3% of the time; consent obtained in only 43.5% of these.

audits.title: Implementation of a data management program in a pediatric cancer unit in a low income country.
audits.setting: Paediatric oncology unit, children's hospital of Tegucigalpa

cycle1.result: Of 652 leukaemia patients, 150 (23%) unregistered and 65 (10%) missing records; in 437 charts protocol information incomplete in 30% and cause of death inaccurate in 18%; other data 99% accurate and 93% to 100% complete.

audits.other_findings: Obstacles included poor records, missing charts and unreliable internet.
audits.citation: Ayoub L, Fú L, Peña A, Sierra JM, Dominguez PC, Pui CH, et al.. Implementation of a data management program in a pediatric cancer unit in a low income country. Pediatr Blood Cancer. 2007;49(1):23-27. doi:10.1002/pbc.20966. PMID: 16862536.

audits.title: Evaluating the accuracy of data entry in a regional colorectal cancer database: implications for national audit.
audits.standard: ACPGBI colorectal cancer minimum dataset (18 key data points)
audits.setting: Regional colorectal cancer database, Digestive Diseases Centre, Brighton

cycle1.result: 83% of data elements present in records; agreement between records and database 61% overall (70% preoperative, 47% operative).

audits.other_findings: Suggests weekly review of entries and/or clinician data entry to improve accuracy.
audits.citation: Kelly M, Lamah M. Evaluating the accuracy of data entry in a regional colorectal cancer database: implications for national audit. Colorectal Dis. 2007;9(4):337-339. doi:10.1111/j.1463-1318.2006.01122.x. PMID: 17432986.

audits.title: Point-of-care outcome assessment in the cancer clinic: audit of data quality.
audits.standard: Agreement with chart review and cancer registry
audits.setting: Department of Radiation Oncology, Princess Margaret Hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: TNM stage recorded in all cases; discrepancy 3-13%; 19 (31%) of 62 outcomes missed in the database.

audits.other_findings: No outcomes incorrectly recorded; new processes introduced to improve completeness.
audits.citation: Wong K, Huang SH, O'Sullivan B, Lockwood G, Dale D, Michaelson T, et al.. Point-of-care outcome assessment in the cancer clinic: audit of data quality. Radiother Oncol. 2010;95(3):339-343. doi:10.1016/j.radonc.2010.03.015. PMID: 20362349.

audits.title: External validation of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database.
audits.setting: 10 randomly selected sites of the STS General Thoracic Surgery Database

cycle1.result: 28 omissions among 559 lobectomy cases, 94.6% agreement with operative logs; overall data accuracy 94.9%; all category agreement rates above 90%.

audits.other_findings: Unsubmitted cases had no mortality or major morbidity, suggesting no gaming.
audits.citation: Magee MJ, Wright CD, McDonald D, Fernandez FG, Kozower BD. External validation of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database. Ann Thorac Surg. 2013;96(5):1734-9; discussion 1738-9. doi:10.1016/j.athoracsur.2013.04.124. PMID: 23998406.

audits.title: Data integrity of the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) clinical registry.
audits.standard: Predefined major and minor discrepancy definitions; case submission within 1 month of discharge
audits.setting: Eight paediatric cardiac intensive care centres (PC4 registry)

cycle1.result: 434 encounters and 29,476 fields audited; overall accuracy 99.1% and major discrepancy rate 0.62%; seven of eight hospitals submitted >90% of cases within 1 month.

audits.other_findings: Accuracy ranged from 96.3 to 99.5% across hospitals; no evidence of selective case omission.
audits.citation: Gaies M, Donohue JE, Willis GM, Kennedy AT, Butcher J, Scheurer MA, et al.. Data integrity of the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) clinical registry. Cardiol Young. 2016;26(6):1090-1096. doi:10.1017/s1047951115001833. PMID: 26358157.

audits.title: Data Quality Improvement and Internal Data Audit of the Chinese Neonatal Network Data Collection System.
audits.standard: Predefined agreement rates for critical, important and less important data elements
audits.setting: 58 tertiary NICUs in the Chinese Neonatal Network (re-abstraction audit)

cycle1.result: Agreement 96.1% overall; 97.2% critical, 94.3% important, 96.6% less important (24,904 fields).

audits.other_findings: Site discrepancy rates ranged from 0.0 to 18.4%.
audits.citation: Sun J, Cao Y, Hei M, Sun H, Wang L, Zhou W, et al.. Data Quality Improvement and Internal Data Audit of the Chinese Neonatal Network Data Collection System. Front Pediatr. 2021;9:711200. doi:10.3389/fped.2021.711200. PMID: 34671584.

audits.setting: All 20 paediatric and adult Swiss cystic fibrosis centres (Swiss CF registry, ECFSPR project)

cycle1.result: Data correctness ≥95% for most variables; low proportion of missing data.

cycle2.result: Availability of genetic source data and informed consents improved.
